                    ### Question
                    Question linked to image nº9 A 35-year-old woman comes to the consultation because she presents chest pain when she is struggling. It does not have cardiovascular risk factors. A systolic murmur is heard in aortic focus that increases with the Valsalva maneuver. The ECG shows sinus rhythm, Q waves, repolarization disorders and left ventricular hypertrophy criteria. In the figure you can see an image of your echocardiography. Point to the FALSE option:

                    ### Options
                    opa. It is a hereditary disease.
opb. This disease is associated with sudden death.
opc. Atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease.
opd. Dyspnea will not appear until the patient develops left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The FALSE option is opc. Atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease. While aortic stenosis and left ventricular hypertrophy can predispose to atrial fibrillation, the statement that atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease is false based on standard consensus. The evidence paths support the relationship between left ventricular hypertrophy and atrial fibrillation but do not specifically address the incidence in this disease.
